clue.text: Dirty film about corruption is man's bag

indicators.note: the scum sits around the other word, wrapping it on both sides

parts.note: scum is a dirty film on a liquid's surface
rot is decay or moral corruption

explanation.surface: A grubby movie about sleaze is apparently just the thing for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical joke: the pouch of skin holding the testes is literally a male bag.

clue.text: Make for swimmers in too deep splashing around

indicators.note: around says the concealed letters are turned round, read right to left
in says the answer lies inside the run of words too deep splashing

explanation.surface: Swimmers out of their depth go splashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashing around' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit backwards inside 'too deeP Splashing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known brand of swimwear is a manufacturer, a make, for swimmers.

clue.text: Viewer's part of subject by Turner

parts.note: re means on the subject of
Tina Turner, the singer

explanation.surface: A gallery viewer looks at part of a painting's subject by J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is the singer Tina Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer here is an eye, and this light-sensitive layer is part of it.

clue.text: See Tim/Dawn, in organisation, one behind the other

indicators.note: organising letters arranges them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Instructions to look at Tim and Dawn, who are organising, queueing one behind the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim and Dawn are colleagues in the sitcom The Office, matching the Wernham Hogg theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem bicycle seats riders in line, so this adverb describes arrangement in single file.

clue.text: Farrow's cry of pain is beastly sound

parts.note: Mia Farrow, the actress
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: An actress's cry of pain sounds like an animal's.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call is the noise of an animal, hence beastly.

clue.text: A student supporter's written about "heartless Gove" for part of curriculum

indicators.note: the supporter is written after, on the subject of, the heartless Gove

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the outer letters of the name Gove remain

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's backer writes about Michael Gove, the former Education Secretary, in a curriculum debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove was a British Education Secretary, which suits the curriculum surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics lessons include this branch using letters for unknown quantities, so it is one school subject component.

clue.text: High fliers upset so Brent unusually receptive

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the airline's letters upside down

parts.note: BA, British Airways, whose planes fly high

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so these letters take an unusual order

explanation.surface: Airline staff are upset, though Brent is oddly open to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Brent is David Brent, the manager in The Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that soaks things up readily is receptive to them.

clue.text: Horse drug found in smallest sample from Godolphin lines

indicators.note: the tiniest sample of a word is its first letter
the drug is discovered inside the other letters

parts.note: RY, railway, is a set of lines
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A racehorse fails a drug test from a Godolphin stable sample.
explanation.walkthrough: Godolphin is a famous racing stable, which is why the horse sense hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a whitish or ash-coloured coat is called by this colour.

clue.text: Succeed in getting Brent's leader to hang up

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ring off is to end a phone call

explanation.surface: David Brent's boss manages to get him to put the phone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish something difficult is to pull it off, achieve it.

clue.text: Sign unions press government to cut predictions

indicators.note: cutting into the sign means going inside it

parts.note: Aries is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: the unions squeeze the government between them

parts.note: U stands for union, so two give UU

explanation.surface: Trade unions lobby the government for cuts in a forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens and portents are signs foretelling the future, so they work as forecasts.

clue.text: Gear, when stripped, can corrode

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer letters, leaving the inside of Gear

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Stripped-down machinery gear might be prone to rust and corrosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into metal is to wear it away chemically, a phrasal synonym for corrode.

clue.text: Working in case Wernham Hogg's closing, taking in secretarial assistant

indicators.note: working means in motion, so the following letters are set to work in a new order
the closing letter of the firm's name Hogg

parts.note: Hogg, possessive dropped

explanation.surface: Office life at Wernham Hogg, the fictional paper firm in the sitcom The Office, as it shuts down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is only a link; its 'in' joins the anagram fodder with 'in case Wernham' and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone device records callers' messages, doing a job a secretary once did.

clue.text: Grind of tutor typing?

parts.note: a don is a university tutor
typing is, whimsically, work done at the keys

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tutor's typing is tedious drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'key work' for typing is not a dictionary phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious hard labour, the drudgery a beast of burden does, is called a grind.

clue.text: Medium for growth: a tabloid in recession

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the tabloid word is read back to front

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper is a growth medium during an economic recession.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories culture bacteria on a jelly made from seaweed, a medium for growing them.

clue.text: With a common focus, Tory wealthy mostly welcome foreign money

indicators.note: the two parts take in foreign money as a guest

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: rich means wealthy
a cent is a coin in the US and eurozone

explanation.surface: Rich Tory donors are happy to take in overseas cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Circles sharing one centre point are geometrically described with this adjective.

clue.text: Around the office we drink

indicators.note: turning letters around rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Around the workplace, staff drink something; here the phrase is a scattering of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with milk added is a common beverage, one specific kind of drink.

clue.text: Drunk single, neat absinthe ultimately and triple from Britney Spears

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: spears pierce and break things apart, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word neat as written, followed by the ultimate letter of absinthe

indicators.note: a triple taken from the front of the name gives its first three letters

explanation.surface: Britney Spears gets drunk on a single neat absinthe and then a triple.
explanation.walkthrough: Britney Spears reads as the pop singer, but Spears is the anagram signal working on what comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a drunkard or habitual tippler is a drunk.

clue.text: Slough was his place — at first job title rejected

parts.note: to place money on a horse is to bet

indicators.note: at first means take only the first letter
rejected means thrown back, so the title word is reversed

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: A man recalls Slough as his old workplace and his first job title.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet John Betjeman wrote 'Slough' ('Come friendly bombs'); Slough is also where The Office is set.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem Slough was written by this Poet Laureate, so it was his.

clue.text: One arguing with Forest manager drawing in league

indicators.note: the ranger draws the league letter inside

parts.note: a ranger manages a forest

explanation.surface: A football club boss rows with the Nottingham Forest manager over a league draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wrangles is quarrelling or disputing noisily.

clue.text: Foreign cup-tie, score one against continental club?

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so these letters are made strange by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A football fan scores a European cup tie against a continental club.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'continental club' looks like a football side but is the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposing the European Union, cheekily called a continental club, is hostile to Brussels.

clue.text: Time sort of right on one Jewish month

parts.note: -ish means sort of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting the timing roughly right for one month of the Jewish calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The first month of the Jewish civil year falls in autumn and opens with Rosh Hashanah.

clue.text: Later: Extras

definitions.meaning: an informal farewell, like 'see you later'
in cricket, byes are extras, runs scored without the bat touching the ball

explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as two byes, cricket runs credited when the ball passes the batter and keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a casual goodbye and a pair of cricket runs not off the bat.

clue.text: Psychologist's French article extracted from confusing mass

indicators.note: something extracted is pulled out, here removed from the tangle

parts.note: a jungle is a tangled, confusing mass
le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A psychologist's work in French is pulled from a confusing mass of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung, the Swiss founder of analytical psychology, is a famous psychologist.

clue.text: Bent copper doesn't start off with rest in New York

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the word copper loses its starting letter
the rest goes inside New York's abbreviation

parts.note: to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman takes it easy, enjoying a break in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like crooked, describing the copper, but it means a tendency. OPPER (copper without its start) is shuffled by 'off' into PROPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination, a leaning toward something.

clue.text: Palm Sunday's parting hymn

indicators.note: parting means splitting the palm word to make room

parts.note: S is short for Sunday

explanation.surface: The closing hymn on Palm Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs of praise from the Book of Psalms are sacred hymns.

clue.text: Fancy '50s hairdo that is dovetailed

indicators.note: dovetailed means interlocked, so the two pairs of letters alternate

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
the DA, or duck's arse, was a 1950s quiff hairstyle
the second letter of the DA hairstyle

explanation.surface: An elaborate 1950s hairstyle, all neatly interlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Interleave IE with DA, alternating letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, a thought that occurs to someone.

clue.text: Short tune a hit before performance

indicators.note: short means cut, so the tune word loses its last letter

parts.note: a melody is a tune
to ram is to strike or hit

explanation.surface: A brief tune becomes a hit before a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts run MELOD, RAM, A: the 'a' trails the hit rather than leading it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, sensational play is a type of stage performance.

clue.text: Concerning addiction without it?

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the clue's 'it' is taken away from the addiction word

parts.note: a habit is an addiction

explanation.surface: A question about addiction and what happens when you go without.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment for addicts is meant to leave them free of their drug, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Report managed to back pay

indicators.note: going back means the managed word is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
a rate is a level of pay

explanation.surface: A journalist reports that management backs a pay deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount events is to report them, telling a story.
